idea: Dossier is a report of record: a paper page that reads like a feature, cut by full-bleed ink sections that hold the evidence. Every claim wears its class (intel, plan, verified), outcomes land as stamps, what is not yet known is a redaction bar, and one lime stroke marks the word the whole document turns on. It is built for documents that will be argued with.
use_for: Implementation plans, incident reviews and post-mortems, board reports, pilot evaluations, long features that make a case and show their working.
avoid_when: Playful or warm subjects, product marketing, anything that must feel light; dashboards scanned in seconds (the condensed caps are for reading, not glancing).
principles_headline: Five rules for a document that will be argued with.
principles: Reading sections sit on paper in Newsreader. Evidence sits on night: figures, ledgers, code, frames. The reader always knows which they are in.
Intel is dashed, plan is filled, verified is double-ruled. A sentence without a tag is a sentence without standing.
Sections divide with a 3px ink rule; everything inside divides with a hairline. Nothing else separates.
The highlighter goes under one word per page, the word the argument turns on. A second stroke cancels the first.
Decisions, verdicts and verifications land as a rotated stamp. The stamp is the receipt; the prose explains it.
voice: Declarative, past tense for evidence, future tense for plan: "Eight evenings were counted. The ninth will be."
Name the base of every percentage: "36 of 640 visitors returned a card."
Mark assumptions as assumptions, in the open: "Assumed until a Recon task confirms it."
No adjectives of confidence. The class tag does that work.
colour_headline: Paper, ink, one violet, one lime.
colour_note: Day first: paper ground, ink type, violet for the brand and the evidence series, lime as the highlighter. Night inverts the page: the ink page becomes the ground and paper panels become the inset. Status colours always carry a word; the class tags carry no colour at all.
chart_note: Violet is the measured series, ink the baseline, caution the assumed line, positive the verified one. On night the series lift but keep order. Grid in line, axes in ink, direct labels where they fit.
type_headline: Archivo shouts in caps, Newsreader reads, Plex Mono files.
type_note: Archivo is a variable face: display roles run at 62% width and 900 weight with .8 leading; interface text runs at normal width. Newsreader carries every paragraph meant to be read. IBM Plex Mono carries eyebrows, tags, figures in ledgers, and the stamp.
space_headline: A 4px base, hairlines inside, three pixels between.
space: Tag padding, gap between a tag and its word.
Default stack gap; card padding on small screens.
Card padding; gap between facts-rail rows.
Section padding on wide screens; the ink sections breathe.
edges: Sections, cards, callouts, ledgers, stamps. Square.
Fields, buttons, tags: barely rounded, so corners stay sharp at small sizes.
Ink, between sections and under the masthead.
Line, inside sections: ledger rows, facts rail, card divisions.
Tags and outline buttons use a 1.5px currentColor border; verified tags use a 3px double.
depth: Nothing floats. Cards are flat on paper with a hairline.
10px 10px 0 violet: the one offset shadow, reserved for the case-file card and the date slip.
A currentColor bar at .95em replaces what is not yet known. It is a shape, not a blur.
motion: Buttons and rows invert: paper to ink or lime, 120ms linear. No lift.
Nothing moves; the fill darkens one step.
3px violet outline, 2px offset. On night, lime.
Stamps land: scale from 1.15 to 1 with a 160ms ease-out when revealed (kit reveal-scale). Nothing else animates in.
None. A dossier does not blink.
Bars draw from the baseline over 240ms; lines do not animate.
components_headline: The kit wears paper and violet; the classes carry the case.
components_note: Kit components take Dossier through the contract: paper grounds, violet primary, lime accent, 2px radius. The tags, stamps, redaction, section head and case-file card are authored classes (do-*) written against the hand variables, so they port.

fields_note: Fields sit on paper-raised with a 1.5px ink edge and a 3px violet focus outline. Labels are mono caps above the field. The segmented control fills its active segment with lime.

chart_comp_note: Charts take violet first, ink second. On night they sit in a paper-less panel: axes in on-night, grid in night-muted at 30%.
table_note: Ledgers are mono figures on hairline rows, caps heads under a 3px rule, no zebra. A class tag may sit in the first column.

motifs_note: Dossier draws with a 2px square-capped ink line and 45° hatch where another system would use a flat fill, so figures look traced from evidence rather than painted. Its own devices below.

dos: Open every section with the numbered head and a 3px rule.
Tag every claim: intel, plan or verified.
Put evidence on night and narrative on paper.
One lime stroke per page, under the word that matters.
donts: No colour on class tags; the border style is the meaning.
No rounded cards, no shadows except shadow-file.
No second accent: violet is the brand, lime is the marker, nothing else.
No blur: what is unknown is redacted, not faded.
binding_losses: The night section (ink inside paper), the class-tag border grammar, the lime highlighter, the redaction bar and the violet file shadow have no contract slot. They are carried as --ds-* properties and the do-* classes; kit components follow paper, ink and violet but not the three-pixel rule.
footer: Day first, Night second. Fonts: Archivo 400–900 (variable width), Newsreader 300–500 + italics, IBM Plex Mono 400/500/700, all Google-hosted.

queries.series: select phase, failed, class, step from rows order by step
queries.table: select step, phase, minutes, requests, failed, class from rows order by step
queries.totals: select sum(minutes) as minutes, sum(requests) as requests, sum(failed) as failed, round(100.0*sum(failed)/sum(requests),1) as failed_pct, 4 as actions, 3 as verified from rows

data.tab_body: Narrative: what happened, in order, on paper.

hand.headline: A traced line and a hatched fill.
hand.note: Dossier draws the way evidence is drawn: a 2px square-capped ink line around everything, 45° hatch in violet where a fill would go, flat sunk paper for the quiet parts, and mono caps for every label. Nothing is painted; everything looks traced from a source. The subject is the artifact's; the hand is this.
rules: 2px ink, square caps and joins, on every shape.
Never flat for the subject: 45° hatch in violet at a 6px pitch. Ink hatch for the second series.
Flat sunk paper, no hatch, so the hatched parts read as the data.
Mono caps at 11px; the display face, condensed, for the one number.
Paper-raised behind every drawing; on night, the drawing inverts with the page.
None in the drawing. A stamp beside it may land.

tpl.slide_body: Across the fourteen-minute window. Nine in ten of them in the six diagnose minutes, before the index was named.
tpl.ed_headline: The index that was never written
tpl.ed_deck: Two people pressed Book in the same twenty milliseconds. The database said yes to both. Here is what the logs can prove about the fourteen minutes that followed.
tpl.ed_byline: Platform on-call · Rev. 02 · 2 Oct 2026 · verified 3 of 4
tpl.ed_body: At eleven o'clock the booking API began returning two confirmations for one slot. The on-call engineer saw the first alert at 11:03, which the edge logs verify. For the next six minutes the team looked at the cache, which held a 97% hit rate throughout and was not the cause. The partial unique index that should have refused the second write had been written in a migration plan and never in a migration.
steps: One hundred requests in the window.
Each square is one request. Violet hatch is a failure; sunk paper is a success. The pattern is the finding.
Sixty of them failed in six minutes.
The diagnose phase is where the window was lost. The mitigate phase, four minutes, failed only fifteen.

tpl.landing_headline: Say what you know. Show how.
tpl.landing_sub: Plans, reviews and reports where every claim carries its evidence class, every outcome lands as a stamp, and the one word that matters is marked.
features: Intel, plan, verified. Dashed, filled, double. No colour needed.
Narrative reads on paper; evidence sits on night. The reader always knows which.
Decisions land as stamps, with a date. The prose explains; the stamp is the receipt.
